content.text: {"narrative":[{"claim":"India faced a data fragmentation challenge in WASH measurement, with fragmented definitions, reporting formats and data systems making it difficult to measure progress consistently and spotlight inequalities.","cites":["risk:44"]},{"claim":"The Government of India launched the Swachh Bharat (Clean India) Mission in 2014, and 110 million toilets were constructed under it.","cites":["fact:01a126fa-f450-72e0-ab2e-5337393aa52d","kpi:156"]},{"claim":"India reached 580 million people with improved drinking water and 550 million people with basic sanitation in the last 10 years.","cites":["kpi:153","kpi:152"]},{"claim":"In 2024, 59.3 million people in India accessed safely managed water and 17.9 million accessed safely managed sanitation.","cites":["kpi:160","kpi:159"]},{"claim":"The Government of India invested over $120 billion in water and sanitation.","cites":["kpi:155"]},{"claim":"India launched the Jal Jeevan (Water is Life) Mission to achieve universal access to safe and adequate drinking water.","cites":["fact:01a126fa-f451-72b9-826e-fffe994c4da6"]}]}
